newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: IMF welcomes Pakistan's economic reforms package.
newsitem.headline: IMF welcomes Pakistan's economic reforms package.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Saturday an economic reforms package announced by Pakistan could provide a basis for adoption of a new structural adjustment loan.

"The successful implementation of the government's reform measures accompanying macro-economic improvements will provide a basis for the adoption of multi-year arrangements under the concessional Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) and Extended Fund Facility (EFF)," an IMF statement said.
On Friday, Pakistan announced an economic reforms package which cut several taxes and sought to boost revenue with more efficient tax recovery and an enhanced tax base.
The economic package followed the collapse of an IMF standby loan, suspended earlier this month after Pakistan failed to meet agreed targets.

IMF Director, Middle Eastern Department, Paul Chabrier welcomed the reforms package as "bold and comprehensive" and said the measures would help structure Pakistan's economy more efficiently and improve public finances.
"The timely implementation of these wide-ranging policies should significantly strengthen the basis for high and sustainable growth in Pakistan in the context of financial stability," Chabrier said.
He said the policy dialogue with the Pakistan authorities would focus on progress in the reforms and on preparations for the next step in signing an agreement on the ESAF.
The IMF had already agreed to continue monitoring the economy and possibly start talks on an ESAF programme later in the year.
